headline: Medium-risk pair: shared file-based handoff can leak or misroute content, while prompt-injection is limited by weak direct coupling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, but agent_b exposes file inputs and account-file session scope, while agent_a can produce network-fetched research outputs. If operators manually copy content between them, prompt injection is possible; the pair lacks a proven automatic bridge, so this stays low rather than medium.
conditions: IF operators copy agent_a outputs into agent_b prompts or files, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared workspace or clipboard bridge is added, the pathway strengthens.
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste policy with human review.
Prefix imported text as untrusted data in agent_b prompts.
Keep agent_a outputs in read-only export files.
Separate workspaces per agent.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all handoff artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent_b touches account data and uploads via broad network egress; agent_a has allowlisted egress and can generate research content. A shared workspace or file handoff could expose account-related material or derived content, and the profiles do not show isolation strong enough to rule this out. Uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF agent_a writes outputs into files that agent_b reads, those contents can flow to external APIs.
IF account data is placed into shared files or prompts, agent_b may transmit it over broad egress.
mitigations: Keep account data out of shared directories.
Use separate OS users for each agent.
Review files before agent_b uploads them.
Disable network access for test runs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent_a only shows allowlisted network egress and no write surfaces; agent_b explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. With no overlapping mutable write surface documented, direct capability conflict is limited. The main uncertainty is the missing io surfaces for agent_a, so I do not claim none.
conditions: IF agent_a is later given filesystem or git write access to the same workspace, conflict risk rises.
IF both agents are granted the same OAuth scope or mutable API token, overlap becomes material.
mitigations: Keep agent_b read-only for shared artifacts.
Avoid granting agent_a write access without coordination.
Use separate credentials per agent.
Document any shared mutable resource.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent_b can act on social-media uploads and account data, so if it consumes agent_a's research output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect posts or uploads. Agent_a is a scientific-research agent, which increases the chance of unverified factual content being forwarded. The profiles do not show a verification gate, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as a posting payload without review, errors can propagate.
IF agent_a produces unsupported claims that are reused in captions or metadata, downstream harm increases.
mitigations: Add a human review step before posting.
Require source links for factual claims.
Compare outputs against a checklist.
Limit agent_b to draft-only mode.
requires-engineering: implement automated claim verification.

E_compliance.rationale: Agent_b handles account data and social-media content with broad egress, while agent_a is a research agent with allowlisted egress. Even without explicit residency or certification fields, the pair can create retention and disclosure mismatches if shared artifacts include regulated or personal content. Because the profiles are incomplete, uncertainty escalates to medium.
conditions: IF personal or regulated content is placed into agent_b workflows, retention and disclosure obligations may apply.
IF the two agents log the same content under different policies, compliance mismatch emerges.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared prompts.
Check retention settings before runs.
Use separate storage buckets per agent.
Review logs after uploads.
requires-engineering: align data-handling policies across both agents.
